evidence:wdr2026_policy.title: World Drug Report 2026 annex 11.1: cannabis regulation

evidenceClaims.claim: Canada's federal Cannabis Act and Cannabis Regulations were implemented on 17 October 2018.
evidenceClaims.caveat: Nationwide federal implementation; provincial rules differ.

evidenceClaims.claim: UNODC reports Colombia and Ecuador as cocaine shipment departure countries serving North America and Europe.
evidenceClaims.originalExcerpt: Colombia and Ecuador supplying North America and Europe
evidenceClaims.evidenceBasis: UNODC WDR 2026 textual summary of reported seizure departure patterns
evidenceClaims.caveat: Reported departure and destination patterns are aggregated over 2020-2024; no shipment-level country-pair counts or annual flows are published here.

evidenceClaims.claim: UNODC describes Brazil as a significant cocaine departure point for flows to Europe, Africa and Asia.
evidenceClaims.originalExcerpt: Brazil playing a key role in flows to Europe, as well as Africa and Asia
evidenceClaims.evidenceBasis: UNODC WDR 2026 textual summary of reported seizure departure patterns
evidenceClaims.caveat: Brazil may be a departure or transshipment country rather than the cultivation origin; this source does not quantify annual bilateral flows.

evidenceClaims.claim: Germany's Cannabis Act came into force in April 2024, with grower clubs following in July 2024.
evidenceClaims.originalExcerpt:
April 2024: Cannabis Act
July 2024: Grower clubs
January 2025: Central Criminal Register and Educative Measures Register
evidenceClaims.caveat: The annex describes separate implementation stages and does not imply a general retail market.

evidenceClaims.claim: Luxembourg implemented its limited non-medical cannabis reform on 21 July 2023.
evidenceClaims.caveat: The annex limits cultivation, possession and use to residences; this is not a commercial retail legalization.

evidenceClaims.claim: Malta implemented its non-medical cannabis reform on 18 December 2021.
evidenceClaims.caveat: The annex describes nonprofit clubs and home cultivation, not general commercial retail sales.

evidenceClaims.claim: Afghanistan was the leading reported methamphetamine departure country for seizures reported in Asia in the 2021-2024 period.
evidenceClaims.originalExcerpt: Afghanistan was the main country reported in Asia
evidenceClaims.evidenceBasis: UNODC WDR 2026 textual summary of reported seizure departure patterns
evidenceClaims.caveat: This is a ranking of reported countries of departure, not a measured Afghanistan-to-any-destination annual flow.

evidenceClaims.claim: Mexico was the dominant reported methamphetamine departure country for seizures reported in the Americas in the 2021-2024 period.
evidenceClaims.evidenceBasis: UNODC WDR 2026 textual summary of reported seizure departure patterns
evidenceClaims.caveat: This is a regional departure ranking; it neither identifies every destination nor quantifies bilateral flows.

researchModelResults.outcome: World Bank general-population homicide rate in year t+1, per 100,000
researchModelResults.predictor: log(1 + latest published UNODC cocaine seizure kg in year t)
researchModelResults.caveat: Retrospective, ecological, noncausal association. Seizures reflect enforcement/reporting, not trade volume or route exposure; homicide is general-population, not drug-attributed. Latest available UNODC annex editions and 2026 World Bank retrieval may revise past years.

researchDefinitions.label: Published national seizure revision
researchDefinitions.selectionRule: Same ISO3, drug and observation year; at least two editions, oldest kg > 0; retain both edition inputs
researchDefinitions.interpretation: Source revision, not a real-world flow change. Country-of-seizure reporting and enforcement matter.

researchDefinitions.label: Cocaine seizures and next-year homicide pair
researchDefinitions.formula: value = World Bank general-population homicide rate in year t+1; model predictor = log(1 + UNODC cocaine seizure kg at t)
researchDefinitions.selectionRule: Latest published annex edition for country/year/drug; matched non-null World Bank next-year homicide; observed years only
researchDefinitions.interpretation: Ecological, retrospective association. No route exposure or drug-specific mortality is observed.
